facts.statement: Acronemus lived during the Middle Triassic period in Switzerland.
facts.quote: Acronemus is an extinct genus of euselachian from the Middle Triassic of Switzerland.

facts.statement: Acronemus is classified as Euselachii incertae sedis because it possesses a mix of features resembling both hybodontiforms and neoselachians.
facts.quote: Though originally placed within Ctenacanthiformes, it is now considered Euselachii incertae sedis, due to its mixture of features similar to hybodontiforms and neoselachians.

facts.statement: A 2018 study suggested Acronemus belongs to the family Tristychiidae and is closely related to the genus Tristychius.
facts.quote: A 2018 study considered it to be closely related to the early Carboniferous genus Tristychius as part of the family Tristychiidae as a basal euselachian

facts.statement: Acronemus was a small animal that grew to be between 30 and 35 centimeters long.
facts.quote: It was a small animal measuring 30 - 35 cm long.

facts.statement: Fossil evidence showed that teeth originally named Acrodus bicarinatus and fin spines named Nemacanthus tuberculatus belonged to the same animal, leading to the name Acronemus tuberculatus.
facts.quote: Associated material showed they were the same animal, with the older specific epithet (tuberculatus) taking precedence.

facts.statement: Fossils of Acronemus are found in the Anisian-age Grenzbitumenzone, also known as the Besano Formation, at Monte San Giorgio.
facts.quote: Acronemus is found in the Anisian-age Grenzbitumenzone (also known as the Besano Formation) of Monte San Giorgio.

facts.statement: Acronemus belongs to the parent group Euselachii.
Acronemus is classified within the class Chondrichthyes.

rejected.statement: The genus Acronemus was described by Rieppel in 1982.
